lens: Signal-processing / quantization theory: closed-loop vs open-loop predictive coding, companding optimality (Bennett/Panter-Dite, Gish-Pierce), dead-zone quantizers, error-bounded uniform quantization, per-variable rate allocation.
overall_assessment: The single proposal that matters most is P1 (closed-loop error-feedback encoding): every other improvement is noise until the encoder tracks the decoder's state, because the current open-loop cumprod decode (core_enhanced.py lines 634-636) turns per-step quantization error into an unbounded multiplicative random walk — that is the entire 3.8e95 MetroPT-3 failure and most of the 108-vs-0.004 Air Quality gap, and anchors are an expensive bandage (float64 lists serialized as JSON decimal text in PNG tEXt chunks, ~20 bytes/value). But P1 alone only bounds error; it does not win rate-distortion, because the second structural defect is that mu=255 companding deliberately spreads symbols across the full [0,255] range with near-maximal entropy (~7.3-8 bits/symbol), so PNG DEFLATE has nothing to exploit — the measured lossy ratios (0.114 for 8-bit ≈ 0.91 bytes/sample out of 1) confirm the entropy stage is doing almost nothing. The shipping combination is P1+P2: closed-loop encoding of scale-relative residuals through a per-variable uniform dead-zone quantizer with step derived from a user error bound, plus a sparse outlier escape — this is exactly the architecture (predict → error-bounded uniform quantize → entropy code) that makes SZ win, and Gish-Pierce guarantees uniform-quantize+entropy-code is within 0.254 bits/sample of the rate-distortion optimum, so no companding scheme can beat it by more than that. Fold P4 (per-variable step allocation) into P2's step rule — it is three lines. Implement P3 (adaptive residual domain) as the default residual definition inside P1/P2 since it removes the near-zero epsilon/auto_offset heuristics for free. P5 (Lloyd-Max) is only worth doing for the strict marketing constraint that the raw 8-bit PNG with no entropy recoding must be the payload; at fixed 8 bits it recovers ~2-4 dB but never closes the gap P2 closes. Benchmark honestly by sweeping epsilon in P2 against the existing zfp_sweep/sz3_sweep in baselines.py at matched RMSE, reporting encode MB/s with and without numba, since P1's sequential loop is the one real cost.

proposals.name: P1: Closed-loop (DPCM) error-feedback encoding
proposals.mechanism: Move the quantizer inside the prediction loop. Today _compute_raw_percent_grid computes P[i,t] = 100*(X[t]-X[t-1])/max(|X[t-1]|,eps) entirely from ORIGINAL data (core_enhanced.py lines 297-323), and decode applies quantized factors by cumprod (lines 634-636). The per-step quantization error e[t] in log-domain accumulates as sum(e[1..t]): a random walk with sqrt(t) growth in the zero-mean case, and exponential exp(mu*t) divergence whenever the per-step error has any bias mu != 0 — which it always does here, because (a) clamping is one-sided on trending data, (b) E[log(1+P_hat/100)] != log(1+P/100) even for symmetric quantization noise (Jensen), and (c) the mu-law round-trip is not mean-preserving per bin. That is exactly the MetroPT-3 RMSE 3.8e95 at t=1.5e6. Closed-loop fix: the encoder maintains the decoder's reconstruction xhat and encodes the change relative to xhat, not the original: r[t] = 100*(X[t]-xhat[t-1])/max(|xhat[t-1]|,eps); quantize r; update xhat[t] = xhat[t-1]*(1+r_hat[t]/100). Every step's quantization error is fed back and corrected on the next step, so the pointwise relative error is bounded by ONE quantizer step forever: |X[t]-xhat[t]| <= |xhat[t-1]|*C_i*Delta_max/200 at every t. Drift is structurally impossible; anchors (anchor_interval, the re-propagation loop at lines 639-657, and the JSON anchor payload) become dead code and their overhead disappears.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is the classic open-loop vs closed-loop DPCM result: open-loop DPCM accumulates quantization noise with variance growing at least linearly in t; closed-loop bounds it at one step, independent of t. The competitors TRACQ loses to (SZ3, Gorilla) are both closed-loop by construction. On Air Quality (T~9000), the reported RMSE 108.3 for Enh-8b+Anchors is dominated by inter-anchor drift, not quantizer resolution: with mu=255, 8 bits, clamp C~50%, the near-zero reconstruction step is C * (2/255) * ln(1+mu)/mu ~ 0.0085% relative per step — a per-step error floor around 1e-4 of signal, i.e., O(0.1) absolute on channels of scale ~1000. Closed-loop collapses RMSE from drift-dominated (10^2) to step-bounded (10^-1..10^0) with ZERO bytes added — in fact bytes are removed because anchors go away. Decoder needs no change at all: the existing cumprod recursion IS the decoder that the closed-loop encoder simulates.
proposals.expected_gain: MetroPT-3: unanchored divergence (RMSE 3.8e95) eliminated outright; RMSE bounded near the anchored figure (~1.7) or better while removing the anchor payload — anchors every 100 steps cost 8*n_vars bytes per anchor binary, but are actually stored as JSON decimal text (~18-22 bytes/float) in the tEXt chunk via codec.py, so on 1.5M steps x 15k anchors this is a double-digit percentage of the artifact; expect ratio to improve from 0.0297 toward ~0.02 at equal-or-better RMSE. UCI Air Quality: RMSE 108.3 -> order 0.1-1 at the SAME 0.114 ratio (2-3 orders of magnitude RMSE reduction, no rate cost). This one change moves every point of the TRACQ rate-distortion curve down by 10^2-10^95 depending on T.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In core_enhanced.py add closed_loop=True to __init__ and a _quantize_closed_loop(bits) used by quantize_8bit/quantize_16bit. Sequential over t, vectorized over variables: xhat = baseline.copy(); for t in 1..T-1: r = 100*(X[:,t]-xhat)/np.maximum(np.abs(xhat), eps); r = np.clip(r, -C, C); y = compander.compress(r/C); q[:,t-1] = np.round((y+1)/2*levels); yq = q[:,t-1]/levels*2-1; xhat = xhat*(1+compander.expand(yq)*C/100). reconstruct_from_quantized is untouched (the cumprod path already implements this exact recursion), so old artifacts stay readable via a metadata flag "closed_loop": true. Clamps C_i must now be computed from a first open-loop pass over raw pct (existing _compute_adaptive_clamps) — fine, since closed-loop residuals have almost the same marginal when tracking is good. Speed: wrap the t-loop in numba.njit — the file already probes HAS_NUMBA (lines 21-25); pure-numpy fallback is ~5-15 s per 1.5M steps, numba ~0.1 s.
proposals.risk: Slope overload: if the clamp C_i is too tight, closed-loop lags a fast ramp for several steps (bounded, but locally worse than open-loop). Mitigate by computing C_i with headroom (existing 1.1x max blend already does this) or with P2's outlier escape. Encode throughput drops without numba, which hurts the paper's MB/s table — must report both paths. Also eps-floor interaction: when |xhat| ~ eps the relative step explodes; P3's residual domain removes this entirely.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Fully. The stored object is still the (n_vars x T-1) quantized grid, same dtype, same PNG path in codec.py; only WHICH values land in each pixel changes (residuals w.r.t. reconstruction instead of original — visually near-identical when tracking is good, and anomalies still show as bright/dark pixels).
proposals.interactions: Prerequisite for everything: P2's error-bound guarantee only holds inside a closed loop; higher-order predictors (delta-of-delta, linear extrapolation 2*xhat[t-1]-xhat[t-2]) drop into the same loop by replacing the prediction term and each halving of residual variance buys ~1 bit/sample at equal distortion; anchors and their JSON cost are deleted, simplifying the container.

proposals.name: P2: Error-bounded uniform dead-zone quantizer with sparse outlier escape (replaces mu-law + percentile clamp)
proposals.mechanism: Replace the mu-law compander + percentile clamp + full-range mapping with a per-variable UNIFORM scalar quantizer whose step is derived from a user-specified error bound, SZ-style, running inside P1's loop. User supplies eps_abs and/or eps_rel; per-variable step delta_i = 2*max(eps_abs, eps_rel*S_i) with S_i a robust scale (std or MAD). Encode: r = X[:,t]-xhat; k = round(r/delta_i) (dead-zone variant: k = sign(r)*floor(|r|/delta_i + 0.5 - dz) with dz~0.2 to widen the zero bin); code = k + 2^(bits-1) stored as uint8/uint16; xhat += k*delta_i, guaranteeing |X[t]-xhat[t]| <= delta_i/2 <= eps pointwise for all t. If |k| exceeds the code range (spike beyond ~127 steps for 8-bit), emit an outlier: append (var_idx int32, t int32, X[i,t] float32/64) to a binary side list, set code to a reserved escape value, and reset xhat[i] = stored value (state reset keeps the bound). Symbols now concentrate massively at the center code (mid-gray): smooth channels emit long runs of 128, which DEFLATE/Zstd crush. This simultaneously fixes brief failure modes 1 (RMSE gap), 3 (lossy barely beats lossless), and 5 (no error bound).
proposals.why_it_wins: Two theorems do the work. (a) Gish-Pierce: uniform scalar quantization followed by ideal entropy coding is within 0.254 bits/sample (1.53 dB) of the Shannon rate-distortion function of ANY smooth source at moderate-to-high rate — so no companding scheme (mu-law, Lloyd-Max, NF4 quantiles) can beat uniform+entropy-coding by more than a quarter bit. The current design does the opposite: mu-law is a variance-equalizing compander that pushes the symbol distribution TOWARD uniform over [0,255] (~7.3-8 bits/sample entropy), which is precisely why the measured 8-bit ratio 0.114 barely beats the 0.125 raw-byte floor and barely beats lossless Delta+Zstd (0.12-0.24) — TRACQ currently pays ~8 bits/sample for what SZ3 encodes in 0.5-3 bits/sample. (b) Rate-distortion accounting at matched RMSE on Air Quality: to hit ZFP's RMSE 0.004 needs eps ~ 0.007 (RMSE = delta/sqrt(12) = eps/sqrt(3) = 0.577*eps for uniform noise); hourly deltas on the PT08 channels (scale ~1000, step-to-step moves of tens) give |k| up to ~10^3, i.e., ~11-12 bits raw range, but the residual ENTROPY after prediction is far lower (Laplacian-like, most mass within a few steps) — realistically 5-9 bits/sample after Zstd, i.e., ratio 0.08-0.14 vs ZFP's 0.273 at the same RMSE. Structural edge over ZFP: ZFP's 4x4 block transform on a (vars x time) array mixes 4 UNRELATED variables per block along the vars axis, wasting rate; TRACQ's per-variable temporal prediction never pays that cost. This is the honest path to a genuine Pareto win on the real UCI datasets.
proposals.expected_gain: UCI Air Quality: at matched RMSE 0.004, expected ratio 0.08-0.14 vs ZFP 0.273 — a ~2x rate win; at matched ratio ~0.114, expected RMSE ~0.003-0.01 vs current 108.3 (4+ orders of magnitude). At looser bounds (eps_rel=1e-2), expected ratio 0.02-0.05 — decisively below lossless Delta+Zstd (0.12-0.24), fixing failure mode 3. MetroPT-3: eps_abs tuned to RMSE 1.55 (PAA's figure) should land near ratio 0.005-0.015 (mostly-zero codes + Zstd) vs PAA 0.0007 — PAA may keep the extreme-ratio end (it discards per-timestep resolution, which TRACQ must keep), but TRACQ becomes Pareto-competitive at every operating point that preserves temporal resolution, which is the paper's claim. Plus a marketable guarantee ZFP-tolerance also has but current TRACQ lacks: max abs/rel error <= eps at EVERY point.
proposals.implementation_sketch: In core_enhanced.py add error_bound: Optional[dict] (e.g. {"abs": 0.01} or {"rel": 1e-3}) and bits in {8,16}. Compute S_i = np.std(X, axis=1) (or MAD); delta_i = 2*max(eps_abs, eps_rel*S_i); store delta_i list in metadata. Encoder (numba/numpy loop as in P1): r = X[:,t]-xhat; k = np.rint(r/delta); ovf = np.abs(k) > kmax (kmax=126 for 8-bit, reserving 0 and 255 as escape); for overflow vars: outliers.append(i, t, X[i,t]); k[ovf]=ESCAPE; xhat[ovf]=X[ovf,t]; else xhat += k*delta; codes[:,t-1] = k + 128. Outliers packed binary with np.ndarray.tobytes into a private PNG chunk or the Zstd container header — NOT JSON text (also migrate baseline/clamps from tEXt JSON decimal to binary; codec.py currently serializes everything as JSON strings, lines 22-30). Decoder: k = codes.astype(int) - 128; recon = np.cumsum(k*delta_i[:,None], axis=1) + baseline[:,None] with outlier overrides applied by segment-resetting the cumsum (np.add.at trick or per-segment cumsum) — fully vectorized, no loop needed on decode. Add eps values to a sweep script mirroring zfp_sweep in baselines.py for honest RD curves.
proposals.risk: 8-bit code range (+/-126 steps) is tight at small eps on spiky channels -> outlier list balloons and ratio suffers; fall back to 16-bit codes (entropy coding makes the wider range nearly free) or auto-select bits from the k-histogram. The 'adaptive quantization' narrative changes from companding to adaptive step + dead zone + escape — reviewers may ask how it differs from SZ1.x with a previous-value predictor: the honest answer is the 2D image artifact, per-variable scale adaptation, and the relative-error mode; the paper must own that. Zstd on codes will beat PNG DEFLATE by 10-30%; keeping PNG as the required VIEW while Zstd is the SIZE artifact needs a clear story (container.py already supports both).
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Yes, and arguably improves it: the code grid is still one uint8/uint16 pixel per variable per timestep; mid-gray = no change, and anomalies/spikes stand out against a flat gray background far more legibly than the current full-range mu-law texture. Escape pixels (0/255) visually flag exactly the extreme events. PNG remains a first-class output via the unchanged codec.py path.
proposals.interactions: Requires P1's loop for the pointwise guarantee. Symbol concentration at the center code is precisely what unlocks the entropy stage (whether PNG DEFLATE, Zstd, or a future range coder) — this proposal is the quantizer half of the SZ recipe and any entropy-stage proposal from another lens multiplies with it rather than adding. Better predictors (delta-of-delta) shrink |k| entropy further inside the same loop. Subsumes dead-zone quantization as a parameter (dz) rather than a separate mechanism.

proposals.name: P3: Scale-relative residual domain (divide by per-variable scale, not by previous value)
proposals.mechanism: Change WHAT is quantized: define the grid pixel as the change relative to the variable's characteristic scale, P[i,t] = (X[i,t] - xhat[i,t-1]) / S_i, with S_i = std or MAD of variable i, instead of dividing by the previous VALUE max(|X[t-1]|, eps). Reconstruction becomes additive (xhat[t] = xhat[t-1] + P_hat*S_i) instead of multiplicative cumprod. This deletes the entire near-zero pathology: the epsilon floor in _compute_raw_percent_grid (line 320), the auto_offset/_compute_value_offsets machinery (lines 210-248, which shifts channels by 2*|min|+eps and stores offsets in metadata), and the near_zero_std_factor heuristic all become unnecessary, because the denominator S_i is a constant, strictly positive, well-conditioned number. It also removes the multiplicative error compounding channel even in a hypothetical open-loop mode (additive accumulation is a plain random walk, no exponential mode) and removes the Jensen bias of E[prod(1+e_t)].
proposals.why_it_wins: The percent-change-of-previous-value transform is the direct cause of failure mode 4 (near-zero blow-ups patched with offsets) and an amplifier of failure modes 1-2: dividing by a signal-dependent quantity makes the quantizer's effective step in OUTPUT units proportional to |X[t-1]|, so the same 8-bit budget delivers wildly different absolute accuracy along one channel's trajectory, and RMSE (an absolute metric — the one the paper is judged on) is dominated by the high-|X| stretches where the step is coarsest. Quantization theory says: to minimize output MSE, the step in output units should be (near-)constant — which is exactly delta_i = const per variable, i.e., this proposal combined with P2. The auto_offset hack also silently corrupts the relative-change semantics (a channel shifted by 2*|min| no longer shows its true percent changes in the image). Dividing by S_i keeps every pixel a dimensionless, cross-variable-comparable relative change — the visual semantics the paper wants — while making the codec numerically boring in the best way.
proposals.expected_gain: On channels that cross or approach zero (the motivation for auto_offset; present in Air Quality's sensor channels after calibration offsets), removes the pathological error concentration entirely — expect the per-channel RMSE spread to tighten by 1-2 orders of magnitude on the worst channels at unchanged rate. Eliminates ~40 lines of offset heuristics and their metadata. In combination with P2 it is what makes a global eps_rel produce uniform per-channel normalized error, directly improving the SMAPE and Pearson-rho columns of the paper's metric table (these are scale-normalized metrics currently wrecked by near-zero channels).
proposals.implementation_sketch: In core_enhanced.py add residual_domain: Literal['pct','scale'] = 'scale'. In the P1/P2 encoder loop replace the division: r = (X[:,t]-xhat)/S (S = np.maximum(np.std(X,axis=1), tiny) computed once, stored in metadata as "scales": S.tolist()). Decode: xhat[t] = xhat[t-1] + k*delta*S_i — with P2 this is the same vectorized cumsum decode. Keep 'pct' mode for backward compatibility and for the paper's ablation table. Delete (or bypass) auto_offset when residual_domain='scale'. ~30 lines net.
proposals.risk: Semantics shift: a pixel is now 'change in units of channel volatility' rather than 'percent of previous value'. For truly multiplicative processes (prices), pct/log-domain is the better residual; keep both modes and select per dataset (or per variable via a cheap encode-both-pick-smaller trial). Reviewers may see the scale-relative grid as closer to z-scored deltas — the defense is that per-timestep relative-change visualization is preserved and improved (no blow-ups saturating the colormap).
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Yes — the artifact is still a per-timestep 2D grid of dimensionless relative changes, one pixel per variable per timestep. Visual anomaly detection improves: near-zero channels no longer saturate to the clamp rails (whole rows pinned at 0/255 in the current scheme convey nothing), and cross-channel comparison becomes meaningful because all pixels share the same unit (sigmas of change).
proposals.interactions: Pure synergy with P1 (removes the eps-floor instability inside the closed loop) and P2 (makes delta_i = 2*eps_rel*S_i exact rather than approximate, and makes the additive cumsum decode trivial). Slightly reduces the benefit of log-domain mode (use_log_domain), which can be deprecated. No conflicts.

proposals.name: P4: Per-variable rate allocation via the step rule (reverse water-filling for free)
proposals.mechanism: Replace the two rigid operating points (8-bit or 16-bit for ALL variables, per quantize_8bit/quantize_16bit) with a continuous per-variable step assignment that implements optimal bit allocation implicitly. Two modes: (a) error-bounded mode — delta_i = 2*max(eps_abs, eps_rel*S_i) as in P2, which IS reverse water-filling for the corresponding weighted-MSE criterion (equal per-variable distortion in the chosen norm); (b) fixed-rate mode — user gives a byte budget; choose a single scale factor lambda and set delta_i = lambda*S_res_i (S_res_i = residual std of variable i), then bisect on lambda until the PREDICTED entropy sum(H_i(delta_i))*T/8 meets the budget, where H_i is estimated from the histogram of k = round(r_i/delta_i) — a cheap numpy computation (one np.histogram + dot product per candidate lambda, ~6 bisection steps). Classical high-rate allocation b_i = b_mean + 0.5*log2(sigma_i^2/geomean(sigma^2)) falls out automatically because equal delta-to-sigma ratio equalizes per-variable entropy differences at exactly that rate split.
proposals.why_it_wins: Air Quality mixes channels of scale ~1 (CO(GT) in mg/m^3) with channels of scale ~1000 (PT08 raw sensor counts). Giving both 8 bits over their clamp ranges wastes rate on whichever channel has low residual entropy and starves the other: at fixed total rate R, MSE-optimal allocation beats equal allocation by the factor arithmetic-mean/geometric-mean of the per-variable residual variances — for variance spreads of 10^4-10^6 across channels (typical here) that is 3-10 dB of output SNR, i.e., 1.4-3x RMSE reduction at identical byte count, or equivalently ~0.5-1.5 bits/sample saved at equal RMSE. It also gives the paper a continuous rate dial (any target ratio) instead of two points, which is what a credible rate-distortion CURVE against zfp_sweep requires.
proposals.expected_gain: At fixed rate on heterogeneous datasets (Air Quality, MetroPT-3's mixed pressure/temperature/current channels): 1.4-3x RMSE reduction vs equal-bits, on top of P1+P2 gains. In error-bounded relative mode: 10-30% ratio reduction at the same reported RMSE because low-volatility channels stop consuming full-range codes. On homogeneous synthetic data: ~no gain (honest null result to report). Also fixes the paper's inability to place TRACQ points at arbitrary ratios for Pareto comparison.
proposals.implementation_sketch: Sits entirely inside P2's setup code in core_enhanced.py. Mode (a) is already the P2 step rule (3 lines). Mode (b): r0 = np.diff(X,axis=1) (open-loop residual proxy is fine for allocation); S_res = np.std(r0,axis=1); def predicted_bytes(lam): H=[entropy(np.histogram(np.rint(r0[i]/ (lam*S_res[i])), bins=...)[0]) for i in range(n)]; return sum(H)*T/8 + overhead; bisect lam over ~6 iterations to hit the budget; then run the P2 closed-loop encode with delta_i = lam*S_res_i. Store delta_i in metadata ("deltas": [...]). ~40 lines, no new dependencies.
proposals.risk: Entropy prediction from the open-loop residual proxy under-estimates closed-loop code entropy slightly when tracking error is non-negligible (small bias, one-sided: actual bytes come in a few % high; acceptable, or do one refinement pass). If a future entropy stage compresses across variables (2D context), per-variable entropy sums are only approximate. Degenerate channels (S_res ~ 0, e.g., constant sensors) need a delta floor to avoid huge k ranges from numerical noise — one np.maximum.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Yes. Codes stay in one uint8/uint16 grid; each row simply has its own documented step delta_i in metadata (exactly like the existing per-variable clamps list). Rendering is unchanged; a viewer can multiply rows by delta_i*S_i for a physically-scaled view.
proposals.interactions: Pure parameterization of P2 — no new encode path. Synergy with any entropy stage (allocation is computed IN entropy units, so it remains near-optimal whatever coder follows). With better predictors, recompute S_res from the new predictor's residuals — one line. No conflicts; skip mode (b) at first ship if time-constrained, since mode (a) captures most of the win on the paper's datasets.

proposals.name: P5: Per-variable Lloyd-Max / optimized-mu codebook for the strict pure-PNG-8 mode (lowest priority)
proposals.mechanism: Only for the operating point where the raw 8-bit PNG with exactly 256 levels must itself be the payload (no entropy recoding beyond PNG's DEFLATE, viewability paramount): replace the fixed mu=255 compander with a per-variable 256-level Lloyd-Max quantizer trained on that variable's residual distribution (1D k-means: init centers at empirical quantiles i/256 — the NF4-style start — then ~15 iterations of assign-via-np.searchsorted / update-via-np.bincount means), or the cheaper variant: per-variable mu_i selected from a small grid {15, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511, 1023} by directly minimizing round-trip reconstruction MSE. Codebook (256 float32 per variable) or mu_i scalar goes in metadata; decode is a table lookup centers[q].
proposals.why_it_wins: Bennett's high-rate theory: optimal companding places quantizer point density proportional to f(x)^(1/3). Fixed mu=255 is a log-law tuned for speech at 13-bit dynamic range; here the clamp sits at the 99.5th percentile, which for a Laplacian residual (scale b) is ~5.3b, and mu=255 then spends HALF of all 256 levels on |x| < 0.059*C ~ 0.31b — i.e., 50% of the codebook covers only ~27% of the probability mass, over-resolving tiny changes whose output-MSE contribution is negligible while starving the mid-range (0.3b-2b) where most of the MSE lives. Lloyd-Max reallocates by f^(1/3) and is MSE-optimal for the fixed level count. But note the ceiling: at 8 bits the gap between a well-fit compander and Lloyd-Max is only ~2-4 dB, and by Gish-Pierce the P2 uniform+entropy design beats BOTH — this proposal exists solely because the pure-PNG-8 constraint forbids relying on the entropy stage.
proposals.expected_gain: 1.5-3 dB output SNR (RMSE / 1.2-1.4) at identical 8-bit rate on Air Quality-like residual distributions, assuming P1 closed-loop is already in place (without P1 the gain is invisible under drift). Compression ratio unchanged (slightly worse PNG DEFLATE, since Lloyd-Max symbols are more uniform than mu-law's — measure it; typically <5% ratio penalty). Codebook overhead: 1 KB/variable as float32, negligible for T > ~10k; for many-variable short series, share one codebook trained on pooled S_i-normalized residuals (1 KB total, ~0.5 dB of the gain sacrificed).
proposals.implementation_sketch: New class LloydMaxQuantizer in core_enhanced.py beside MuLawCompander: fit(residuals) -> centers (np.quantile init, loop: edges=(centers[:-1]+centers[1:])/2; idx=np.searchsorted(edges, r); centers=np.bincount(idx, weights=r, minlength=256)/np.maximum(np.bincount(idx, minlength=256),1)); encode(r) = np.searchsorted(edges, r).astype(np.uint8); decode(q) = centers[q]. Plug into the P1 loop in place of compander.compress/expand (fit on first-pass open-loop residuals). Metadata: "codebooks": centers per variable (float32 list) or "mu_per_var": [...]. ~60 lines. The adaptive-mu variant is ~15 lines (grid search with vectorized round-trip MSE).
proposals.risk: Strictly dominated by P2 whenever an entropy stage is allowed — do not let it compete for implementation time. Codebook trained on open-loop residuals mismatches closed-loop residuals slightly (minor). Empty-bin handling in k-means needs care (keep previous center). Per-variable codebooks bloat metadata for wide short series. Reviewer risk: 'you reinvented Lloyd 1957' — frame it as the ablation baseline that motivates the uniform+entropy design, which is a nice paper narrative (show mu-law < Lloyd-Max < uniform+entropy on the same RD plot).
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Fully — output is still one uint8 grid per PNG, 256 levels, directly viewable; pixel intensity ordering is monotone in the residual, so the visual semantics are identical to the current mu-law image.
proposals.interactions: Requires P1 (under open-loop drift its 2-4 dB is invisible). Mutually exclusive with P2 per operating point (they are two different quantizers for the same slot): ship P2 as the flagship RD mode and P5 as the 'pure image' mode. Mildly conflicts with the entropy stage (more-uniform symbols compress worse in PNG); no conflict with P3/P4 (both compose: Lloyd-Max on scale-relative residuals with per-variable codebooks is exactly P3+P4+P5).
